title: ACP profile / programme configuration (ACP-1.1 amendment candidate implementation)
description: Machine-checkable contract for an ACP profile document (for example acp/acp.yml, parsed to JSON). Layer: Implementation. STATUS: implements ACP-1.1 (feat/acp-1-1-normative-amendments@1bda3e99), paired with envelope 0.3.0. Conformance requires format-assertion enabled in the validator (M1); see README, 'Required normative amendments before adoption'. A profile selects policy inside the space Core allows: it may tighten Core requirements but must never redefine Core meanings. This schema is generic: no organization, agent, repository or path is hardcoded. It validates shape and internal consistency of policy, not whether the policy is wise or whether the declared accounts exist. Note on repository references: the profile MAY use its binding's native repository form (for example owner/name) because a profile names its binding; the Core envelope may not, and uses a portable reference instead.

acp.description: ACP Core version this profile targets, as major.minor (ACP-1.1 section 16.1, amendment A20).

spec.description: Version of the specification document the profile was written against.

binding.description: Named platform binding and its version, for example github@0.1.0. Binding identity belongs in the profile; binding rules do not belong in Core.

schema_compatibility.description: Which published schema, if any, the profile author believes implements the protocol version they target. `none` is an honest and common answer.

profile.description: Conformance profile name. Generic profiles are ACP-0 through ACP-3; an organization may name its own.

identity.description: Declared trust level of actor attribution. Recommended: a profile that claims separation of powers while every agent shares one account is overstating its guarantees, and the protocol should say so out loud.

trust_level.description: 1 self-declared, 2 shared account, 3 distinct accounts, 4 signed machine identity, 5 organization-managed credentials.

ids.description: Identifier policy. This is the ONLY place naming policy lives: Core accepts any stable opaque token (amendment A12). A validator that checks envelopes without also loading the active profile cannot enforce anything here.

work_item_pattern.description: Regular expression the programme work item identifiers must match. Checked here for well-formedness via format: regex, WHICH IS ONLY ENFORCED IF THE VALIDATOR HAS FORMAT-ASSERTION ENABLED (M1). Conformance to this schema requires it; see README, Conformance requirements. Applying the pattern to envelopes is a separate profile-aware pass that does not exist yet.

reserved.description: Identifiers owned by another namespace (typically a product roadmap) that must never be used as work item identifiers.

agents.description: Declared participants. uniqueItems catches exact duplicates only: two entries sharing an id but differing elsewhere are NOT detectable by JSON Schema. See README, 'What this schema cannot validate'.

roles.description: Protocol capabilities per role: which event types a role may emit. Distinct from permissions, which govern effects on the world.

approve_gates.description: Gates this role may consent to (A7). Replaces the approve:<gate> capability form. That these names correspond to declared gates is referential integrity: a profile linter checks it, this schema cannot (M4).

permissions.description: Platform permissions: what an actor may do in the world. Default deny is the only safe default for a system where some actors are language models.

require_claim_reference.description: ACP-1.1 amendment A18: heartbeat and release must name the claim whose lease they act on.

invalidation.description: Freshness policy. 'invalidation' names the policy; 'freshness' names the derived state of an assertion. Keeping the two words apart is deliberate.

revalidate_resets_ttl.description: ACP-1.1 section 6.3: revalidation carries the verdict to a new SHA but does NOT restart the review TTL. Chained revalidation would otherwise keep a three-week-old review alive forever, which is what rule R4 exists to prevent.

revalidate_same_actor_only.description: ACP-1.1 section 6.3: only the author of the original assertion may revalidate it. Anyone else is making a new assertion, which is a review.

stale_counts_for_gates.description: Must be false to satisfy Core invariant 'stale evidence does not satisfy a gate'.

self_review.description: Must be forbidden: Core forbids an agent independently approving its own delivery for the same basis.

allow_empty_unverified.description: ACP-1.1 amendment A19: `unverified: []` is admissible and means 'nothing left to verify'. Omitting the key remains non-conformant.

require_adversarial_declaration.description: ACP-1.1 section 5.3: every review states whether it is adversarial. Optional, the flag could simply be omitted to escape the falsified requirement.

independence_guaranteed.description: Whether review independence is actually guaranteed. Must be false below identity.trust_level 3: with a shared account the binding cannot tell two agents apart, so 'nobody reviews what they delivered' is honour system. A profile that claims otherwise is overstating its guarantees.

silence.description: What the absence of a human answer means. A profile must state this; leaving it undefined is how a multi-agent system stalls on one person.

never_default.description: Capabilities that silence can never grant. Must include authorize: Core requires that silence never authorizes irreversible or sensitive action.

never_default_actions.description: Concrete actions that may never be the outcome of silence, whatever the question's declared kind (amendment A15). This list exists because the envelope schema can only refuse a silent default on a question EXPLICITLY classified as kind=authorization. A question that requests a deployment while declaring itself kind=decision is syntactically impeccable and semantically an authorization; no schema can tell the difference. This list gives a semantic validator the concrete vocabulary to catch it, and gives a human reviewer a short list to check by hand in the meantime.

require_touches_in.description: Event types that must carry a declared write surface. These are event type names. Since ACP-1.1 amendment A7 the capability names ARE the event type names, so the two registries cannot diverge; the pre-A7 capability spelling is listed only in the prohibited-alias table of ACP-1.1 section 5.3.

allOf.$comment: Automated reconciliation is an implementation, and an implementation must be named before it is trusted.

extensions.description: Single container for local extensions (L1, ACP-1.1 section 5.2.3). Same grammar as the envelope: ^x-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$. Loose x- members at the profile root are no longer accepted, so the rule is identical in both documents and a reader needs one habit, not two.

automation.description: Declared automation posture. Stating its absence explicitly is what makes the absence auditable.

implementation.description: Required when automation is enabled: what runs, who owns it, and what it is allowed to decide.

allOf.$comment: Enabling automation without naming what implements it is the single most dangerous profile error: it authorizes machine action with no accountable component.

eventType.description: Event type names. Deliberately duplicated from envelope.schema.json#/$defs/eventType rather than $ref'd across files: a cross-file reference would force every consumer of this schema to resolve and register the envelope schema, and profile documents are frequently validated alone.
eventType.$comment: CATALOGUE PARITY (conformance requirement C1, amendment A16): this enumeration MUST be the same set as envelope.schema.json#/$defs/eventType, and both files MUST carry the identical digest below. The digest is the sha256 of the comma-joined sorted list with no spaces. Two digest strings can be compared at a glance; two 27-item lists cannot. A release in which the two digests differ is non-conforming and must not be adopted. catalogue-digest: sha256:046f7cadad317948c7a92a808bade47bbbdf61bdb467ce26a49891da730e0e91

capability.description: A protocol capability. ACP-1.1 amendment A7: capability names ARE event type names, plus veto. There is no translation between the two registries, so they cannot diverge. The pre-A7 capability spelling for `spec` is gone, as is the `approve:<gate>` form: `approve` is a plain capability and which gates a role may consent to is declared in roles.<role>.approve_gates. Platform abilities such as running a shell are NOT capabilities; they belong in agent.capabilities_extra.
capability.$comment: CATALOGUE PARITY (C1, A16): this list is the event catalogue plus veto. catalogue-digest: sha256:046f7cadad317948c7a92a808bade47bbbdf61bdb467ce26a49891da730e0e91

handle.description: Platform account, or a @TODO- placeholder while unassigned. A placeholder is honest; a shared real account presented as separate identities is not.

capabilities_extra.description: Platform abilities, not protocol capabilities. Deliberately loose: this is where 'can run a shell' lives.

permissionEntry.description: Three admissible forms. A bare mode; a list of roles allowed to perform it; or an expanded object able to express irreversibility, whose internal contradictions ARE checked.

allOf.$comment: Forbidden but granted to roles is a contradiction, not a nuance.
An irreversible action cannot be freely allowed; it needs authorization or prohibition.

gateRequirement.description: Exactly one condition per entry, so a gate reads as an ordered conjunction of single facts.

automationSlot.description: Either the explicit absence marker, or a list of named components.
